content.title: About
content.content: Chipotle dip is a creamy sauce made from sour cream and mayonnaise, flavored with smoked chipotle pepper, garlic, lime, and spices. It has a mildly spicy, smoky taste and is perfect for serving with chips, vegetables, tacos, and other Mexican dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chipotle is a smoked, dried, and canned jalapeño pepper that gives the dip its distinctive smoky aroma.
The original recipe was created in the United States in the 1970s as an alternative to traditional salsa.
The sauce is often used as a marinade for chicken, fish, and seafood.
In the US, chipotle dip ranks among the top‑10 most popular fast‑food sauces.
There is a low‑fat version that replaces mayonnaise with yogurt or kefir.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Smoked chipotle peppers contain vitamin C and carotenoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Sour cream and yogurt provide probiotics that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Egg‑based mayonnaise supplies a modest amount of vitamin B12, essential for nervous system function.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Sour cream is a good source of calcium, which supports bone health.

items.title: Moderate healthy fats
items.content: Most of the fat in the dip is monounsaturated, which is considered heart‑friendly.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Mayonnaise contains eggs, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The creamy base makes the dip calorie‑dense; portion control is advised, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Added salt can be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Spicy flavor
items.content: Those sensitive to heat may experience stomach discomfort after consuming the dip.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve chipotle dip as a sauce for nachos, tortillas, veggie sticks, grilled chicken, burgers, or as a salad dressing. It can also be mixed into burritos or used as a marinade.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the dip refrigerated in a sealed container. Once opened, it stays fresh for 5‑7 days. Discard if it develops a sour smell or changes color.
